result.title: Can AI agents make law? Evaluating AI legal relevance and creativity
result.comment: 25 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Data, prompts and transcripts: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23435854
result.summary: Large language models, the artificial intelligence (AI) systems behind modern chatbots, are trained on vast amounts of legal text, but can they build on it to write law for situations that text never anticipated? In this study, we analyse AI agents' ability to draft a hypothetical "Constitution" for a "community of AI agents". We design "constitutional assemblies" in which a single language model plays several characters that debate to produce a draft constitution. We find that the assemblies converge on a robust floor of legal provisions, and generate a wide variety of different proposals around it, including several AI-specific provisions with no equivalent in human law. Looking more closely at the "creativity" of these AI agents, we find different levels: most proposals combine existing concepts and themes from human constitutions with AI-specific vocabulary. We introduce a measure of this recombination, which helps identify and highlight the most novel legal material. This study reveals a ceiling on AI creativity: the agents extend familiar legal ideas to new situations, but they do not work through what those situations would change. Although current AI models can help develop new laws, they still depend on human legal reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究让单个语言模型扮演多个角色组成「制宪会议」进行辩论，生成面向 AI 智能体社区的假想宪法草案，并提出一种衡量提案对既有法律概念重组程度的指标，以评估 AI 的法律相关性与创造力上限。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究主题为法律文本起草与多角色辩论式生成，既不涉及视觉或多模态信息保留，也没有推理期 latent 状态、证据获取或停止决策等机制；其「重组式创造力」度量虽涉及生成新颖性，但与 LVR 的状态表示与评价问题缺少可核查的具体接口，故不入选。
